implementation_notes: A Swift forwarding member is either a one-line method - func cancel(id: OrderID) -> CancelResult { repo.cancel(id: id) } - or, when the delegate owns the value, a read-only computed property, var count: Int { repo.count }; there is no delegation keyword and no compile-time member forwarding, so composition means declaring each forwarded member and letting the protocol conformance keep its signature honest. @inline(__always) is only an optimization hint, and Objective-C style forwarding (forwardingTarget(for:)) exists only for NSObject subclasses through the message runtime, so it is not a general replacement. What makes the level idiomatic rather than manual is the computed-property form: a delegated attribute costs one line and no stored state.
pitfalls: A computed forwarding property re-evaluates on every access: let c = svc.count snapshots a value, while repeated svc.count in a loop keeps calling the delegate.

@inlinable/@inline(__always) are hints with real consequences - @inlinable exposes the body and its dependencies across modules - and whole-module optimization usually inlines one-liners without them.

A protocol-witness call can reach an extension default implementation instead of the concrete one-liner when the value is used through an existential, so the code that runs may not be the code you wrote.
